chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Bashir al-Dahhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Abu Jameela from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) from Jabir ibn Abdullah who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the enemy of Allah is carried to his grave, he calls out to his pallbearers, "Do you not hear me, O my brethren? I am complaining to you what your wretched brother has fallen into. The enemy of Allah deceived me, so he imprisoned me and did not release me, and swore to me that he was an advisor to me, so he overwhelmed me."'

"And I complain to you of the world which deceived me until when I was greedy to it, it knocked me down. And I complain to you of the selfish friends who gave me hope, then disavowed from me and abandoned me. And I complain to you of the children whom I protected and preferred them over myself, so they consumed my wealth, and betrayed me. And I complain to you of wealth which I prevented from it the Right of Allah, so its consequences were upon me and its benefits were for others. And I complain to you of a house which I spent upon it my earnings and it became a dwelling for others."

"And I complain to you of the prolonged boarding in my grave calling out to me: 'I am a house of insects! I am a house of darkness, and the loneliness, and the straitness! O brothers! Withhold me whatever you are able to and be cautioned of the likes of what I face, for I have received news of the Fire, and the disgrace, and the belittling, and the Wrath of the Almighty, the Compeller.'

O my regret upon what I neglected regarding the Side of Allah! And O prolonged wailing! So there is not for me a sympathetic intercessor to be merciful to me. So, if there was a possibility of return for me I would be from the Believers'.
ai.seo_question: What does the deceased complain about in the grave according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of *Barzakh* (the intermediate realm) where the deceased's spiritual state is manifested through a resemblance of their worldly attachments, specifically wealth and children. It serves as a potent reminder of *Al-Ghurur* (deception by the world) and the ultimate futility of material accumulation when one neglects the rights of Allah, emphasizing the Shia emphasis on preparing for the grave through righteous deeds and sincere faith.
